Three claims currently in doc 34's approved-claims register — cleared for market-facing use today — are not supported by any code that exists. controlDefectsFoundAndReproduced.title: canon-gate M5 PLAN-ROW validation is INERT for every OPS-17 G-row (fail-open)
controlDefectsFoundAndReproduced.rawOutput:
M5 real G-05      -> exit 0
M5 bogus G-9999   -> exit 0
M5 garbage Q-42   -> exit 0
M5 bogus P-9999   -> exit 2
controlDefectsFoundAndReproduced.sourceLines: canon-gate.ps1:258 `$rowIds = [regex]::Matches($rowsLine, 'P-\d+')`; :259 `if (-not $rowIds) { return 'ok' }`; :256 hardcodes the OPS-16 path; :257-258 return 'ok' if that file is missing or unreadable
controlDefectsFoundAndReproduced.mechanism: This is a design seam, not a coding slip. OPS-17 governing rule 2 deliberately chose the G- prefix so rows 'never collide with the OPS-16 P- rows in a grep, a hook, or a compiler.' That anti-collision choice is EXACTLY what makes the hook blind to them: the hook only greps P-. The program's own namespace-hygiene rule silently disarmed its own gate.
controlDefectsFoundAndReproduced.whyItLookedAlive: P-9999 correctly blocks with exit 2, so the gate appears live under casual testing.
controlDefectsFoundAndReproduced.contractImpact: AGENT_CONTRACT.md section 7 states 'a hand-assembled dispatch missing any marker is blocked by the canon-gate hook.' That guarantee is FALSE for OPS-17 PLAN-ROWs. Every dispatch in this program, INCLUDING this one, passed M5 unvalidated.
controlDefectsFoundAndReproduced.notablyTheCompilerIsStricter: scripts/dispatch.mjs validates G-rows correctly and fails closed (exit 1). The gate that exists to enforce the compiler is weaker than the compiler.
controlDefectsFoundAndReproduced.proposedFix: Make Test-PlanRows plan-aware exactly as dispatch.mjs already is: extract [A-Z]-\d+, resolve the plan file from the row prefix (P- -> OPS-16, G- -> OPS-17), and fail CLOSED on an unknown prefix or a missing plan file instead of returning 'ok'.
controlDefectsFoundAndReproduced.proposedNegativeTest: G-9999 and Q-42 must exit 2; G-05 and P-25 must exit 0; a deleted or renamed plan file must exit 2, not 0.

Three shapes exist across three layers and emit.ts:94-104 carries an explicit shim because the contract DID segment ('workspace') and the engine entityType ('property-workspace') disagree by design. The serving table uses neither (plain uuid defaultRandom(), no did column). This is inherited constraint 6 in the wild.

If a city document family is built, the brokerage family likely needs renaming FIRST — the contract DID segment already disagrees with the engine entityType, and a second family claiming 'workspace' would worsen the collision.

secondFailOpenFoundWhileTesting.cause: both consumers tested amendments by scanning the WHOLE amendment row for the bare token. Amendment A-004 quotes the literal string G-9999 in its prose while documenting the CTRL-1 bug, so G-9999 validated as a real row.

secondFailOpenFoundWhileTesting.fix: anchor to a DECLARATION: a baseline row is the row id in the first cell of its own table row; an amendment row is the row id followed by an add-verb (ADDED|ADD|NEW) inside the amendment Change cell. Never a bare mention.

ctrlFixesApplied.incidentalDefectFixed: canon-gate.ps1 contained 3 non-ASCII punctuation characters (em dashes / smart quotes) introduced by the planner edit. PowerShell 5.1 reads the file as ANSI, and the UTF-8 em dash broke the parse from that line onward, disabling the ENTIRE hook. Found because every negative-test case returned exit 1 instead of 0 or 2. Replaced with ASCII and confirmed with a real PowerShell parser check (PARSE OK). The repo prose convention already bars em dashes; in hook source it has teeth.
ctrlFixesApplied.contractImplication: AGENT_CONTRACT.md section 7 asserts that a hand-assembled dispatch missing any marker is blocked by the canon-gate hook. That guarantee was FALSE for OPS-17 PLAN-ROWs and is now TRUE for both programs. The contract text needs no edit; the code now matches what it always claimed.
